findings.location: Windows branch: #define INVALID_THREAD_VALUE NULL and _startnewthread return
findings.issue: THREAD_ID is HANDLE (a pointer type); INVALID_THREAD_VALUE is NULL, and _startnewthread returns reinterpret_cast<THREAD_ID>(_beginthreadex(...)). reinterpret_cast from uintptr_t to HANDLE is valid, but the source used (THREAD_ID)-0; the change is benign. However StartHttpThread returns pCur->ThreadId after the else-branch where pCur may have been freed on thread-creation failure, which is a source-existing bug, not target-introduced.

findings.location: GetSocketMSS: int opt_len = sizeof tcp_mss; getsockopt(..., &opt_len)
findings.issue: On Windows getsockopt expects int* for optlen, so int is correct; source used unsigned which is also accepted. No compile risk.

findings.location: HTTPSendError: StringCchPrintf with szHTTPDataFmt and %I64u via PRIu64
findings.issue: StringCchPrintf (strsafe) does not support the %I64u format specifier the same way as printf; on MSVC strsafe uses its own formatting and may not handle PRIu64 ("I64u") correctly, producing wrong Content-Length. This is source-existing (source also uses StringCchPrintf with PRIu64).

findings.location: Unix branch removed entirely in target
findings.issue: Target dropped the #ifdef UNIX portability block, so the file is now Windows-only. Profile is C Linux x64 to C++ Windows x64, so this is acceptable, but any non-Windows compile will fail.
findings.repair: No repair; consistent with Windows-only target profile.

limitations: Non-authoritative self-review only; no compile was performed. Findings are limited to visible target-introduced changes; several apparent issues (StringCchPrintf/PRIu64, StartHttpThread use-after-free, ExtractFileName strpbrk NULL deref) are source-existing and not repaired per instructions. reinterpret_cast additions are the main target-introduced edits and appear syntactically valid under MSVC C++17.
